A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDELINE research, with matching architecture and retained experiments. All pages, including appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Atari, MiniGrid and ViZDoom evaluations, architectural ablations, qualitative predictions and training-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds Crafter evaluations, representation probes, generation-error measurements and a Transformer-based architectural comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed Mamba REM, diffusion predictor, shared prediction heads, harmonized losses and actor-critic procedure remain. V2 clarifies parallel execution and timestep sampling; v1's Algorithm 1 already includes burn-in and random target selection. The Transformer variant is an ablation comparator.

E1.justification: V2 adds Crafter's procedurally generated survival, resource collection and crafting tasks, including remembering previously explored terrain (Section 6.2 and Appendix D.11). Atari, MiniGrid and the five ViZDoom scenarios remain. The new probing and MSE analyses reuse existing environments.

E2.justification: V2 adds a Transformer-based REM comparator in Table 8 and the Crafter qualitative comparison, extending v1's architectural comparisons against GRU and LSTM. The retained Atari baseline roster is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include Crafter evaluation with a 1M-step budget, probes using 50 training and 10 validation trajectories with 50/100 training epochs, and pixel-MSE evaluation over specified imagination horizons (Appendices D.6-D.7). The existing Atari budget and default hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds representation probing, quantitative generation-quality analysis, a Transformer-versus-Mamba ablation and Crafter memory/error case studies. Existing GRU/LSTM, cross-attention and harmonizer analyses are largely relocated, not newly introduced. V1's PredictPosition qualitative case figure is omitted.

E5.justification: Appendix D.6 specifies five independent seeds for the new probing experiments. Existing benchmark and ablation reporting retains three-run averages, standard-deviation curves and bootstrap intervals. This does not establish increased run counts for retained experiments; probe uncertainty intervals are not supplied.

E6.justification: Retained Atari tables are numerically unchanged, including EDELINE's 1.866 mean HNS. New Crafter results report 11.5 ± 0.9 versus DIAMOND's 2.8 ± 0.5 (Table 2). Tables 3, 4 and 8 add probing, normalized pixel-MSE of 0.918, and Transformer comparison results. Figure 4 adds ViZDoom learning curves.

T1.justification: V1's Appendix F information-retention theory is removed, including the superiority and information-growth theorems, supporting proofs, critical threshold and optimality conditions. V2 retains the background diffusion/SSM mathematics and actor-critic objectives, largely through relocation and renumbering.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws the introductory contribution claiming provably greater information retention with a linearly growing advantage, replacing it with an empirical memory-enhancement contribution. It extends the headline experimental claims to Crafter and explicitly restricts the introductory Atari superiority claim to methods without look-ahead search.

C2.justification: V2 explains the offsetting world-model and actor-critic timing costs, explicitly acknowledges diffusion's computational overhead, and distinguishes acceptable Crafter prediction discrepancies from memory failures (Appendices A, D.8 and D.11). These add qualifications and mechanism explanations while retaining the central memory-based interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents parallel-scan execution and the probe inputs, prediction heads and feature source. Core hyperparameters and RTX 4090 profiling information remain. Conversely, v1's explicit 4:1 ViZDoom frame-skipping disclosure disappears; this omission does not establish an actual setting change.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Crafter, Transformers, GAIA-1, GAIA-2 and Pandora, with limited expansion of generative-game-engine discussion. The principal positioning around combining diffusion models and SSMs remains. The changed citation style and expanded author names are presentation edits.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, the training explanation is substantially rewritten, and related work is divided into four subsections. Main-text ablations move into Appendix D, which consolidates many previously separate appendices. Background, algorithm and objective sections are also reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure resizing, repositioning and pseudocode reformatting. V2 adds four result tables, ViZDoom learning curves and a Crafter image sequence; it removes the PredictPosition image sequence and harmonizer summary bar chart while relocating other displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central contributions: Crafter and the Transformer ablation broaden the memory tests, while probing and pixel-MSE analyses quantify representation content and prediction fidelity previously supported mainly through architectural arguments and selected images. Withdrawing the broad theoretical guarantee and acknowledging computational costs better calibrate the claims. Some new comparison details remain underspecified, and the frame-skipping disclosure is lost, but these drawbacks are smaller than the gains in direct empirical support.
